keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks Yelang). The page has no infobox or area; 'over 200 years' of activity, 'first described in the 3rd century BC in what is now western Guizhou province'. The discs at Liupanshui and Anshun are a stand-in; the dian dossier's disc (Kunming 120 km) lies to the west.

ledger.note: 281: Yelang first dated in the record. 'Qin sent Sima Cuo, who attacked Ba and eventually won over Ba, Bi and Yelang to Qin alliances' (281 BCE); Chu had earlier sent Zhuang Qiao 'at the head of a military expedition to prevent the state of Qin from annexing these kingdoms' (early 3rd century BC, undated). The page gives no founding: 281 is the first dated mention, a bridge.

ledger.note: 111: Han absorbs Yelang. 'Han absorbed Yelang with the conquest of Nanyue' (111 BC); 'declared their allegiance to Nanyue rule from the start of 183 BC until the end of 111 BC'. The page names no commandery.

wars.outcome: Yelang, a Nanyue vassal from 183 BC, was absorbed by Han in 111 BC when Han conquered Nanyue.
wars.note: Zhang Qian's and Wang Ranyu's 122 BC embassies, a Zangke commandery and the death of King Xing in 27 BC are not on the page. An earlier Qin attempt to annex Yelang failed (Sima Cuo, 281 BCE).

certainty.note: No Yelang boundary is on the page, and its extent is 'believed' to cover parts of four provinces. Soft throughout.

notes: Page opened (1 of 1-2; the earlier dian dossier read the same page for its Zhuang Qiao detail): Yelang. Wikidata id left null (unreachable). START -281 is the first dated mention (confidence 1). The kingdom lasted 'over 200 years', placing its beginning in the 3rd century BC; the page gives no founding. NANYUE: Yelang was a Nanyue vassal from 183 to 111 BC; the nanyue dossier (ea-02) needs a vassal_start 183 and vassal_end 111 with counterpart yelang. HAN: the Yelang page gives no Han commandery; the han-dynasty dossier (ea-02) should carry the gain at 111. REGION: the gazetteer lacks Bijie; the discs follow Liupanshui and Anshun. The extent is far larger than the discs if Sima Qian's 'west of the Mimo and Dian, south of Qiongdu' is right. AREA: none. No rulers.
